children.top_down_role: Prevents valid but weak relaxations from being conflated with exact relaxations.

assumptions_latex: \(F\neq\varnothing\) and \(p^*:=\inf_{x\in F} f(x)>-\infty\).
The problem is a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness semantics for a lower bound in deterministic global minimization.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the minimization problem \(p^*:=\inf\{f(x):x\in F\}\), a scalar \(L\in\mathbb R\) is a correct global lower bound precisely when \(L\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\). Equivalently, \(L\le p^*\). Correctness asserts only validity of the inequality; it does not assert that \(L\) is attainable, sharp, or equal to \(p^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower bound is correct when it does not exceed any feasible objective value, equivalently when it does not exceed the global infimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound Correctness

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

assumptions_latex: Two relaxations concern the same minimization problem with optimal value \(p^*\).
Each relaxation produces a correct lower bound \(L_i\le p^*\), for \(i\in\{1,2\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Relaxation \(2\) is at least as strong as relaxation \(1\) exactly when \(L_2\ge L_1\).

notation.meaning: lower bounds supplied by the two relaxations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength is ordered by lower-bound dominance for a fixed minimization instance.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.5 Relaxation (Successive Outer Approximation) Strategies p. 31

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two valid relaxations of the same minimization problem yield lower bounds \(L_1\) and \(L_2\). Relaxation \(2\) is at least as strong as relaxation \(1\) on that instance if \(L_2\ge L_1\), and it is strictly stronger if \(L_2>L_1\). If both use the same objective over feasible regions \(R_1\) and \(R_2\), then \(R_2\subseteq R_1\) implies \(\inf_{x\in R_2}f(x)\ge\inf_{x\in R_1}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, the relaxation giving the larger valid lower bound is stronger; nesting feasible regions provides a sufficient dominance test when objectives agree.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Strength

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.5 Relaxation (Successive Outer Approximation) Strategies p. 31

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\) and both optimization problems use the same extended-real objective \(f\).
The infima \(p^*:=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\) and \(p_R:=\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\) are well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation is optimal-value exact if and only if \(p_R=p^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value exactness for an outer relaxation using the original objective.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.5 Relaxation (Successive Outer Approximation) Strategies p. 31

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an original minimization problem \(p^*:=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\) and its outer relaxation \(p_R:=\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\) with \(F\subseteq R\), the relaxation is optimal-value exact when \(p_R=p^*\). This equality does not require equality of feasible sets or minimizer sets; a relaxed optimizer may lie in \(R\setminus F\) while attaining the same optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outer relaxation is optimal-value exact when its infimum equals the original problem's infimum, even if its feasible or optimal solutions differ.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Value Exactness

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.5 Relaxation (Successive Outer Approximation) Strategies p. 31

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\) and both problems use the same objective \(f\).
Both argmin sets are defined, possibly as empty sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solution-set exactness holds if and only if \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in R}f(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equality of optimizer sets in the original variable space.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an original feasible set \(F\), an outer relaxed set \(R\supseteq F\), and a common objective \(f\), the relaxation is solution-set exact when \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in R}f(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\). Consequently, every relaxed global minimizer is feasible for the original problem and every original global minimizer remains relaxed-optimal. When the common argmin set is nonempty, solution-set exactness implies optimal-value exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solution-set exactness means that the relaxed and original problems have exactly the same global minimizers; with attained minima, this also gives value exactness.
knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Set Exactness

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Solution Upper Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbent upper bounds for minimization obtained from feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem \(p^*:=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\), a verifiably feasible point \(\hat x\in F\) with finite objective value defines the feasible-solution upper bound \(U:=f(\hat x)\), which satisfies \(p^*\le U\). The point \(\hat x\), its feasibility verification, and the evaluation of \(f(\hat x)\) witness this bound. If \(L\in\mathbb R\) is a correct lower bound and \(\varepsilon\ge 0\) satisfies \(U-L\le\varepsilon\), then \(f(\hat x)-p^*\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, any verified feasible point with finite objective value defines an upper bound. If that upper bound is within a nonnegative tolerance of a valid lower bound, the point is globally near-optimal within that tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The problem is \(p^*:=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\).
A point \(\hat x\in F\) has finite objective value \(f(\hat x)\in\mathbb R\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set \(R\) is an outer feasible-region relaxation of an original feasible set \(F\) when \(F\subseteq R\). Thus every originally feasible point remains feasible in the relaxation, although \(R\) may contain additional points. For a common minimization objective \(f\), this inclusion gives \(\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\le\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\), so the relaxed optimal value is a valid lower bound whenever the infima are defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outer relaxation contains every original feasible point, possibly adding others; minimizing the same objective over it yields a lower bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set \(I\) is an inner feasible-region approximation of \(F\) when \(I\subseteq F\). Every point in \(I\) is therefore feasible for the original problem, but feasible points may be omitted. For a common minimization objective \(f\), \(\inf_{x\in I}f(x)\ge\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\); hence an attained minimizer over \(I\) supplies a feasible-solution upper bound, not generally a lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner approximation contains only original feasible points. Minimizing over it can produce feasible upper bounds but may exclude globally optimal solutions.

source_refs.locator: 3.5 The Global Optimization (GOP) Algorithm p. 84

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p^*:=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\), an optimal-value lower-bound certificate is a witness \(w\) from which a verifier can check that \(L(w)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\). Acceptance therefore establishes \(L(w)\le p^*\). Together with a feasible point \(\hat x\in F\), the inequalities \(L(w)\le p^*\le f(\hat x)\) certify an optimality gap no larger than \(f(\hat x)-L(w)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound certificate is a checkable witness proving a scalar lower bound on the global optimum; paired with a feasible point, it certifies an optimality gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Value Bound Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the system \(Ax\le b\), a vector \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying \(y\ge0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\), and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\) is an infeasibility certificate. Indeed, any putative \(x\) with \(Ax\le b\) would satisfy \(y^{\mathsf T}Ax\le y^{\mathsf T}b<0\), whereas \(y^{\mathsf T}Ax=0\). Verification requires only the displayed matrix-vector products, componentwise sign test, and strict scalar inequality.

knowledge_statements.title: Region-Exclusion Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic exclusion of a search region using a valid regional lower bound and an incumbent upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) over a feasible set \(F\subseteq X\). Let \(R\subseteq X\) be a search region, let \(L_R\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfy \(L_R\leq \inf_{x\in F\cap R}f(x)\), and let \(U=f(\bar x)\) for a known point \(\bar x\in F\). If \(L_R\geq U\), then every \(x\in F\cap R\) satisfies \(f(x)\geq f(\bar x)\). Thus \((L_R,U,\bar x)\), together with verification of the two bounds, certifies that removing \(R\) cannot discard any point strictly improving the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A region may be discarded when its verified lower bound is no smaller than the objective value of a known feasible incumbent.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits the logical claim supported by a regional exclusion certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the setting of regional minimization, a valid certificate \(L_R\geq U=f(\bar x)\) establishes only that no point in \(F\cap R\) has value strictly below \(U\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certifies that a candidate reconstructed from a relaxation solves the original global problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Compact Feasible Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compactness regime for finite-dimensional global minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a problem of minimizing \(f\) over \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), the compact-feasible-region regime holds when \(F\) is nonempty and compact. In Euclidean space this is equivalent to \(F\) being closed and bounded. Compactness localizes every feasible point to a bounded search domain and ensures that every sequence in \(F\) has a subsequence converging to a point of \(F\). Attainment of the infimum additionally requires an appropriate objective regularity condition, such as lower semicontinuity; compactness alone does not impose that condition on \(f\).

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate-Feasibility Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines feasibility relative to an explicit nonnegative constraint tolerance.

\[
F_\varepsilon:=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\leq\varepsilon\ \text{for every }i,

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Underestimator Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certifies a relaxation bound through pointwise objective underestimation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the original minimization problem \(v:=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). Let \(R\supseteq F\) and let \(\ell:R\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) satisfy
\[
\ell(x)\leq f(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in F.
\]
Then the relaxed value \(L:=\inf_{x\in R}\ell(x)\) is a valid global lower bound:
\[
L\leq\inf_{x\in F}\ell(x)\leq v.
\]
Thus the verifiable certificate consists of the inclusion \(F\subseteq R\) and the pointwise underestimator inequality on \(F\); underestimation only on a subset of \(F\) does not certify a global bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective relaxation yields a valid global lower bound when its domain contains the original feasible set and its objective never exceeds the original objective there.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Epigraph-Relaxation Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validates objective and constraint relaxation through epigraph containment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a decision set, let \(F\subseteq X\), and let \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\). Define the restricted epigraph
\[
E:=\{(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb{R}:x\in F,\ t\geq f(x)\}.
\]
For any relaxed epigraph set \(Q\subseteq X\times\mathbb{R}\), the containment \(E\subseteq Q\) implies
\[
\inf\{t:(x,t)\in Q\}\leq\inf\{t:(x,t)\in E\}=\inf_{x\in F}f(x).
\]
Thus epigraph containment certifies a valid lower bound for a simultaneous objective-and-constraint relaxation, including relaxations that do not separate into an outer feasible region and a pointwise objective underestimator.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Envelope Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the convex envelope as the strongest convex objective underestimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and convex, and let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be bounded below. Define the convex envelope of \(f\) on \(C\) by
\[
\operatorname{vex}_C f(x):=\sup\{q(x):q:C\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is convex and }q\leq f\text{ on }C\}.
\]
Then \(\operatorname{vex}_C f\) is the greatest convex underestimator of \(f\): every convex function \(q:C\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(q\leq f\) on \(C\) also satisfies
\[
q\leq\operatorname{vex}_C f\leq f.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\inf_{x\in C}\operatorname{vex}_C f(x)=\inf_{x\in C}f(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a bounded-below real-valued function on a nonempty convex domain, the convex envelope is its greatest convex underestimator and has the same infimum over that domain.

\(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is bounded below

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructs a convex minorant from a difference-of-convex decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex and suppose \(f=g-h\) on \(C\), where \(g,h:C\to\mathbb{R}\) are convex. If an affine function \(u:C\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfies
\[
h(x)\leq u(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in C,
\]

\[
m(x)=g(x)-u(x)\leq g(x)-h(x)=f(x)
\qquad\text{for every }x\in C.
\]
Thus the DC decomposition together with a verified affine overestimator of \(h\) certifies \(m\) as a convex objective minorant and \(\inf_C m\) as a valid lower bound for \(\inf_C f\).

assumptions_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) be a basic closed semialgebraic set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The compactness regime is the geometric condition that \(K\) is closed and bounded. It does not, for a fixed generating family, imply that the associated quadratic module is Archimedean.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric compactness of a polynomial feasible set, distinguished from algebraic Archimedeanity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\). Because \(K\) is closed, it is compact exactly when it is bounded, equivalently when there exists \(R>0\) such that \(K\subseteq\{x:\|x\|_2\le R\}\). Compactness is a property of \(K\). By contrast, the condition \(N-\|x\|_2^2\in M(g)\) is a property of the selected generators; compactness of \(K\) alone need not establish that condition for the given presentation.

children.title: Archimedean–Compactness Implications

assumptions_latex: Let \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0\}\) and suppose its quadratic module satisfies \(N-\|x\|_2^2\in M(g)\) for some \(N>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Then \(K\) is compact. The converse is not automatic for the fixed generators, although an explicit redundant ball inequality can make the augmented quadratic module Archimedean without changing \(K\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-way implication and presentation dependence relating Archimedeanity to compactness.

Hence \(K\) is bounded and, being closed, compact. Compactness of \(K\) does not in general imply that the quadratic module generated by the displayed \(g_j\) is Archimedean. If a valid bound \(R\) is known, adjoining the redundant inequality \(R^2-\|x\|_2^2\ge0\) leaves \(K\) unchanged and makes the augmented module Archimedean.

assumptions_latex: A polynomial optimization problem is posed on a noncompact basic closed semialgebraic set \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Standard Archimedean moment-SOS convergence cannot be invoked solely from feasibility or attainment; validity requires a replacement positivity theorem, weighted construction, coercivity-based compactification, or another independently verified condition.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K\) is noncompact, no quadratic module defining exactly \(K\) can contain \(N-\|x\|_2^2\), since that identity would force \(K\) to be bounded. Thus the standard Archimedean positivity representation and the convergence theorem derived from it are unavailable. Even when \(f^\star=\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\) is finite or attained, those facts alone do not imply convergence of the unmodified hierarchy. Convergence must instead follow from separately verified hypotheses, such as a valid compactification, a non-Archimedean positivity theorem, or a suitable weighted hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a noncompact set, the usual Archimedean hierarchy theorem is unavailable; finite attainment alone does not validate convergence of the unmodified hierarchy.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each admissible order \(d\), let \(p_d^{\mathrm{mom}}\) be the truncated moment relaxation value and \(d_d^{\mathrm{sos}}\) the value of its SOS conic dual. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and suppose \(L_D(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in D\). Then the restriction \(L_D|_C\) satisfies \(L_D(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in C\). Consequently, with \(\beta_D=\inf_{x\in D}L_D(x)\) and \(\beta_C=\inf_{x\in C}L_D(x)\), \[\beta_D\le\beta_C\le\inf_{x\in C}f(x).\] Thus domain restriction preserves the ancestral bound and may strengthen its scalar value even without recomputing the bounding function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower bound valid on a parent region remains valid on every child; minimizing it over the child can only strengthen the scalar bound.

A monotone implementation may safely report \(\max\{\beta_D,\beta_C\}\), since both terms are valid child lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Inherited Ancestral Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inheritance of a minimization lower bound from a parent domain to every descendant subdomain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq X\), let \(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), and adopt \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). For domains \(D'\subseteq D\subseteq X\), suppose \(L_D\in\overline{\mathbb R}\) satisfies \(L_D\leq\inf\{f(x):x\in F\cap D\}\). Since \(F\cap D'\subseteq F\cap D\), the same scalar is a valid inherited bound:
\[
L_D\leq\inf\{f(x):x\in F\cap D'\}.
\]
Thus a descendant may retain every ancestral lower bound; recomputation is needed only to obtain a stronger bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifting Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity of an extended-space relaxation obtained by adding auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq X\), and let \(E\subseteq X\times Y\) be an exact lift satisfying \(F=\pi_X(E)\). If \(\widehat R\subseteq X\times Y\) is a lifted relaxation with \(E\subseteq\widehat R\), then every original feasible point admits a lifted representative in \(\widehat R\). Consequently,
\[
F=\pi_X(E)\subseteq\pi_X(\widehat R).
\]
Hence \(\widehat R\) is valid in extended space and its projection is a valid relaxation in the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended formulation is valid when it contains an exact lift of every feasible point; projecting it then yields a valid original-space relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation of feasible-set containment under coordinate projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\subseteq X\times Y\) be the exact lifted feasible set and let \(\widehat R\subseteq X\times Y\) satisfy \(E\subseteq\widehat R\). Coordinate projection is inclusion-preserving, so
\[
\pi_X(E)\subseteq\pi_X(\widehat R).
\]
Therefore, if \(F=\pi_X(E)\), then \(R=\pi_X(\widehat R)\) is a valid original-space relaxation of \(F\). No convexity, closedness, or uniqueness of the auxiliary coordinate is required for this containment claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting a valid lifted relaxation preserves validity because set inclusion is preserved by projection.

children.title: Lift–Project Consistency

knowledge_statements.title: Lift–Project Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact consistency condition for passing between original and lifted formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F\subseteq X\), a lifted set \(E\subseteq X\times Y\) and lifted objective \(\widehat f:E\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) are lift–project consistent with \(f:F\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) when
\[
F=\pi_X(E),\qquad \widehat f(x,y)=f(x)\quad\text{for every }(x,y)\in E.
\]
Under these conditions,
\[
\inf_{x\in F}f(x)=\inf_{(x,y)\in E}\widehat f(x,y),
\]
and the projection of every lifted minimizer is an original minimizer whenever either infimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lift is consistent when its projection is exactly the original feasible set and its objective agrees with the original objective on every lifted point.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat f(x,y)=f(x)\) for all \((x,y)\in E\).

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Loss Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by distributing projection over intersected lifted constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Projection preserves inclusion but does not generally commute with intersection. Let
\[
E_1=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:y=x\},\qquad E_2=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:y=-x\}.
\]
Then
\[
\pi_X(E_1\cap E_2)=\{0\},
\qquad
\pi_X(E_1)\cap\pi_X(E_2)=\mathbb R.
\]
Thus replacing the exact joint projection by the intersection of separately projected constraints can strictly enlarge the relaxation and destroy all coupling information carried by the shared auxiliary variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection can lose linkage information when intersected lifted constraints are projected separately; exact joint projection is required to retain that information.
assumptions_latex: \(E_1,E_2\subseteq\mathbb R^2\) share the auxiliary coordinate \(y\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample and strict inclusion are correct, but no inspectable citation is supplied. The plain statement should also qualify that joint projection is required for a general guarantee, since separate projections can coincide in special cases.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Elimination Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact elimination of a variable determined uniquely by the retained variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be sets, let \(m\in\mathbb N\), let \(h:X\to Y\), and let \(G:X\times Y\to\mathbb R^m\), with vector inequalities interpreted componentwise. Define
\[
E=\{(x,y)\in X\times Y:y=h(x),\ G(x,y)\leq0\}
\]
and
\[
F=\{x\in X:G(x,h(x))\leq0\}.
\]
Then \(x\mapsto(x,h(x))\) is a bijection from \(F\) to \(E\). Consequently, for every objective \(\widehat f:X\times Y\to\overline{\mathbb R}\),
\[
\inf_{(x,y)\in E}\widehat f(x,y)=\inf_{x\in F}\widehat f(x,h(x)).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a variable is imposed exactly as a single-valued function of the retained variables, substitution eliminates it bijectively and preserves corresponding objective values and the optimal value.

\(y=h(x)\) is imposed exactly throughout the original feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Variable Linkage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Containment condition ensuring that relaxed auxiliary-variable links remain valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
E=\{(x,z)\in X\times Z:x\in F,\ z=h(x)\}

be an exact graph lift. A linkage relaxation \(L\subseteq X\times Z\) is valid precisely when it contains the required graph points, namely \(E\subseteq L\). If additional relaxed constraints form \(Q\subseteq X\times Z\) and also satisfy \(E\subseteq Q\), then
\[
E\subseteq L\cap Q
\quad\text{and}
F\subseteq\pi_X(L\cap Q).
\]
Omitting a link needed for graph containment provides no validity guarantee for the projected formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-preserving scalar transformations of inequalities, equalities, and objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a set, let \(A\subseteq X\), let \(f,g:X\to\mathbb R\), and let \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R\). If \(\alpha>0\), then \(g(x)\leq0\) is equivalent to \(\alpha g(x)\leq0\); if \(\alpha<0\), it is equivalent to \(\alpha g(x)\geq0\). If \(\alpha\neq0\), then \(g(x)=0\) is equivalent to \(\alpha g(x)=0\). For \(\alpha>0\), define
\[
v=\inf_{x\in A}f(x),\qquad v'=\inf_{x\in A}(\alpha f(x)+\beta).
\]
Then
\[
v'=\alpha v+\beta,
\qquad
\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in A}(\alpha f(x)+\beta)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in A}f(x),
\]
with the optimal-value identity interpreted in the extended real numbers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive scaling preserves inequality direction and minimizers; negative inequality scaling requires direction reversal, while every nonzero scaling preserves an equality. Positive affine transformation of an objective preserves minimizers and transforms its optimal value accordingly.
assumptions_latex: \(A\subseteq X\) and \(f,g:X\to\mathbb R\).
\(\alpha\neq0\), with \(\alpha>0\) for objective-order preservation.
\(\beta\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaled constraints have the stated equivalences, and for \(\alpha>0\), \(v'=\alpha v+\beta\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in A}(\alpha f(x)+\beta)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in A}f(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Change Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reformulation under a bijective change of coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Z\) be sets, let \(T:Z\to X\) be a bijection, let \(F\subseteq X\), and let \(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\). Define \(F_T=T^{-1}(F)\) and \(f_T=f\circ T\). Then \(T\) restricts to a bijection from \(F_T\) onto \(F\), and
\[
\inf_{z\in F_T}f_T(z)=\inf_{x\in F}f(x).
\]
Moreover,
\[
T\bigl(\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in F_T}f_T(z)\bigr)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x).
\]
Thus feasibility, corresponding objective values, and global optimality are preserved exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bijective coordinate change gives an equivalent optimization problem, preserving feasible points, corresponding objective values, optimal values, and minimizers.

\(F\subseteq X\) and \(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\).

children.title: Transformation Reversibility

knowledge_statements.title: Transformation Reversibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided inverse condition for reversible transport of formulations and validity statements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z_0\) and \(X_0\) be sets. A transformation \(T:Z_0\to X_0\) is reversible when there exists \(S:X_0\to Z_0\) such that
\[
S(T(z))=z\quad\text{for every }z\in Z_0,
\qquad
T(S(x))=x\quad\text{for every }x\in X_0.
\]
Equivalently, \(T\) is bijective and \(S=T^{-1}\). Under this condition, each set \(A\subseteq X_0\) corresponds bijectively to \(T^{-1}(A)\subseteq Z_0\); each function \(f:X_0\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) transports to \(f\circ T\) and is recovered by composition with \(S\); and an inequality \(g(x)\leq0\) on \(X_0\) corresponds exactly to \(g(T(z))\leq0\) on \(Z_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordinate transformation is reversible exactly when it has a two-sided inverse on the domains being used; sets, functions, and inequalities can then be transported and recovered exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(S\circ T=\operatorname{id}_{Z_0}\).
\(T\circ S=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) is bijective, \(S=T^{-1}\), and transport by composition between \(Z_0\) and \(X_0\) is exactly reversible.

notation.meaning: domains on which reversibility is asserted

knowledge_statements.title: Transformation Singularity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of equivalence when a coordinate map fails to cover the original domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Bijectivity cannot be omitted from an exact coordinate reformulation. Let \(X=Z=[-1,1]\), let \(T(z)=z^2\), and minimize \(f(x)=x\) over \(X\). The original optimum is
\[
\min_{x\in[-1,1]}x=-1,
\]
whereas the transformed problem has
\[
\min_{z\in[-1,1]}f(T(z))=\min_{z\in[-1,1]}z^2=0.
\]
Here \(T\) is noninjective, is not surjective onto \(X\), and has a singular derivative at \(z=0\). Its image omits feasible points needed for the original optimum, so exact reformulation validity fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular, non-bijective coordinate map can omit feasible points and change the global optimum; the squaring map on a symmetric interval demonstrates the failure.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The numerical counterexample is correct, but no citation is supplied. It demonstrates failure caused by lack of coverage of the original feasible domain; noninjectivity and a singular derivative are incidental here. Bijectivity is also stronger than necessary for preservation of an optimal value, so authoritative sourcing and qualification are required.

knowledge_statements.title: Valid-Cut Intersection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and bound monotonicity when valid cuts are intersected with a relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq R\subseteq X\), and let \(C_i\subseteq X\) satisfy \(F\subseteq C_i\) for every \(i\in I\). Then the cut-strengthened set
\[
R'=R\cap\bigcap_{i\in I}C_i
\]
remains a relaxation because \(F\subseteq R'\subseteq R\). For a minimization objective \(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\), its relaxation bound is monotone:
\[
\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\leq\inf_{x\in R'}f(x)\leq\inf_{x\in F}f(x).
\]
Thus intersecting any collection of valid cuts preserves validity and cannot weaken the lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting a relaxation with valid cuts still contains every feasible point and can only improve its minimization lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\subseteq X\).
\(F\subseteq C_i\) for every \(i\in I\).
\(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is minimized.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple Lower-Bound Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise aggregation of finitely many valid lower-bounding functions on one region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a nonempty set, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), and suppose \(\ell_i:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}\) satisfies \(\ell_i(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) and \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Then \(\ell(x):=\max_{1\le i\le m}\ell_i(x)\) is also a valid lower-bounding function: \(\ell(x)\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in X\). Moreover, \(\ell\ge\ell_i\) pointwise for every \(i\), and therefore \(\inf_{x\in X}\ell(x)\ge\max_i\inf_{x\in X}\ell_i(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pointwise maximum of finitely many valid lower bounds remains valid, dominates every constituent bound, and yields a scalar lower bound at least as strong as each constituent minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{N}\) is finite and positive.
Each \(\ell_i\) is pointwise no greater than \(f\) on \(X\).

knowledge_statements.title: Objective–Constraint Relaxation Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity of combining an objective underestimator with an outer relaxation of the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a set, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), and let \(F\subseteq X\) be the feasible set with value \(v:=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). Let \(R\subseteq X\) satisfy \(F\subseteq R\), and let \(\ell:R\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}\) satisfy \(\ell(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\). Then \(L:=\inf_{x\in R}\ell(x)\) satisfies \(L\le v\). Thus objective underestimation and feasible-set outer relaxation compose without invalidating the lower bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposed Relaxation Reassembly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reassembly of componentwise lower bounds for an additively decomposed objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a set, let \(F\subseteq R\subseteq X\), and let \(q\in\mathbb{N}\) be positive. knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Preserving Domain Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact value-preservation criterion for restricting a minimization problem with finite optimal value to a reduced domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a set, let \(F\subseteq X\) be nonempty, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), and suppose \(v:=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\in\mathbb{R}\). For \(D\subseteq X\), the equality \(\inf_{x\in F\cap D}f(x)=v\) holds if and only if, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists \(x_\varepsilon\in F\cap D\) such that \(f(x_\varepsilon)\le v+\varepsilon\). In particular, if the minimum over \(F\) is attained, retaining at least one global minimizer is sufficient for value preservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a problem with finite optimal value, a domain restriction preserves that value exactly when it retains feasible points of every positive optimality accuracy; retaining a global minimizer is sufficient when one exists.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq X\) is nonempty and \(D\subseteq X\).
\(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) and \(v:=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in F\cap D}f(x)=v\iff\forall\varepsilon>0\;\exists x_\varepsilon\in F\cap D:\ f(x_\varepsilon)\le v+\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: A retained feasible point within epsilon of the optimal value.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Preserving Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inheritance of lower-bound validity after safe constraint propagation reduces a search region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a set, let \(F,D\subseteq X\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), and let propagation return \(D'\subseteq D\). Suppose \(U\in\mathbb{R}\) is an incumbent value and every discarded feasible point satisfies \(x\in F\cap(D\setminus D')\Rightarrow f(x)\ge U\). If \(L(D')\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}\) satisfies \(L(D')\le\inf_{x\in F\cap D'}f(x)\), then \(\min\{L(D'),U\}\le\inf_{x\in F\cap D}f(x)\). If \(F\cap(D\setminus D')=\varnothing\), then \(L(D')\le\inf_{x\in F\cap D}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every discarded feasible point is no better than the incumbent, the minimum of the reduced-region lower bound and the incumbent is a valid lower bound for the original region. If no feasible point is discarded, the reduced-region bound itself remains valid.
assumptions_latex: \(F,D\subseteq X\), \(D'\subseteq D\), and \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\).
\(U\in\mathbb{R}\) and \(f(x)\ge U\) for every \(x\in F\cap(D\setminus D')\).
\(L(D')\le\inf_{x\in F\cap D'}f(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Reduction-Certificate Inheritance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A verifiable certificate transferring safe-discard validity to a reduced domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D'\subseteq D\) and let \(U\) be an incumbent value. A reduction certificate consists of finitely checkable inequalities or logical implications establishing \(x\in F\cap(D\setminus D')\Rightarrow f(x)\ge U\). Once verified, the certificate proves that every feasible point with \(f(x)<U\) lies in \(D'\). Hence any subsequent valid lower bound \(L(D')\) yields the inherited bound \(\min\{L(D'),U\}\le\inf_{x\in F\cap D}f(x)\), without revalidating the discarded portion of \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A checkable proof that discarded feasible points cannot improve the incumbent certifies the reduction and lets later reduced-domain lower bounds transfer to the original region.
assumptions_latex: \(D'\subseteq D\) and \(U\) is the value of a feasible incumbent.
The certificate verifiably implies \(f(x)\ge U\) on \(F\cap(D\setminus D')\).
\(L(D')\) is valid on \(F\cap D'\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nested-Chain Exhaustion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustiveness criterion along every infinite chain of descendant regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal{P}_k)_{k\ge0}\) be successive finite subdivisions of a compact metric region \(D\), with every member of \(\mathcal{P}_{k+1}\) contained in a member of \(\mathcal{P}_k\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fair-refinement condition for regions that remain active or are selected infinitely often.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested-Set Bound Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency of a regional lower-bounding operation along shrinking nested feasible regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a metric space, let \(F\subseteq X\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), and let \(D_1\supseteq D_2\supseteq\cdots\) be nonempty compact regions with \(D_\infty:=\bigcap_{k\ge1}D_k\ne\varnothing\). Let \(L\) assign to each such region \(D\) a value in \(\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}\) satisfying \(L(D)\le\inf_{x\in F\cap D}f(x)\), with \(\inf\varnothing:=+\infty\). The operation \(L\) is nested-set consistent on this chain if \(L(D_k)\to\inf_{x\in F\cap D_\infty}f(x)\). If additionally \(D'\subseteq D\Rightarrow L(D')\ge L(D)\), then \((L(D_k))_{k\ge1}\) is nondecreasing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regional lower-bounding operation is nested-set consistent when its bounds on nested compact regions converge to the optimum over their intersection; inclusion monotonicity additionally makes the bound sequence nondecreasing.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a metric space, \(F\subseteq X\), and \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\).
The regions \(D_k\) are nonempty and compact, satisfy \(D_{k+1}\subseteq D_k\), and have nonempty intersection \(D_\infty\).
\(L(D)\le\inf_{x\in F\cap D}f(x)\); inclusion monotonicity is assumed only for the monotonicity conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Spatial Gap Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency of regional relaxations under exhaustive spatial refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be compact, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous, and let \(R_k\subseteq X\) be nested regions with \(\operatorname{diam}(R_k)\to0\). For each nonempty \(R\), let \(L(R)\le \inf_{x\in R}f(x)\) be a valid relaxation bound and let \(U(R)=f(x_R)\) for some \(x_R\in R\). If the relaxation is spatially consistent, meaning \(\inf_{x\in R_k}f(x)-L(R_k)\to0\), then \[0\le U(R_k)-L(R_k)\to0.\] Thus the local feasible upper and relaxation lower bounds coincide along every indefinitely refined branch.

knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchical Gap Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency obtained by increasing relaxation strength on a fixed region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be compact and nonempty, and let \(f:R\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous. Suppose a hierarchy produces valid lower bounds \(L_r(R)\) satisfying \(L_r(R)\le L_{r+1}(R)\le f_R^*\), where \(f_R^*=\min_{x\in R}f(x)\). If the hierarchy is complete on \(R\), meaning \(\sup_{r\ge1}L_r(R)=f_R^*\), then \[L_r(R)\uparrow f_R^*.\] Consequently, for any feasible upper bounds \(U_r(R)\ge f_R^*\) with \(U_r(R)\to f_R^*\), the hierarchical relaxation gap satisfies \(U_r(R)-L_r(R)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monotone complete relaxation hierarchy converges to the regional optimum; paired with convergent feasible upper bounds, its optimality gap vanishes.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Reestimation Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of relaxation validity caused by nonconservative reestimation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A data-driven reestimate is unsafe when it can underestimate the regularity parameter required by the lower-bound formula. For example, on \(R=[0,1]\), let \(f(x)=x\), whose least Lipschitz constant is \(L^*=1\). The Lipschitz lower estimate based at \(c=1\) is \[\ell_{\widehat L}=f(c)-\widehat L\max_{x\in R}|x-c|=1-\widehat L.\] If reestimation returns \(0\le\widehat L<1\), then \(\ell_{\widehat L}>0=\min_{x\in R}f(x)\), so the purported lower bound is invalid. Consequently, reestimation from finite samples requires a certified conservative safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Underestimating a required regularity parameter can raise a purported lower bound above the true minimum; finite-sample reestimation therefore needs a conservative certificate.
assumptions_latex: The lower estimate uses \(c=1\) and \(0\le\widehat L<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_{\widehat L}=1-\widehat L>0=\min_{x\in R}f(x)\), so validity fails.

knowledge_statements.title: Child-Bound Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity of consistent regional lower bounds under branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a parent region \(P\) be partitioned into children \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) with \(C_i\subseteq P\). Suppose the regional lower-bound operator \(L\) is inclusion-monotone: \[A\subseteq B\implies L(A)\ge L(B).\] Then every child bound dominates the parent bound, \[L(C_i)\ge L(P),\qquad i=1,\ldots,m.\] This conclusion applies to exact regional infima and to relaxations whose feasible relaxation sets restrict consistently with the spatial region. Validity alone, \(L(R)\le\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\), does not imply child-bound dominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an inclusion-monotone relaxation, every child region has a lower bound at least as large as its parent's; validity alone is insufficient.

knowledge_statements.title: Ancestor-Bound Inheritance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation of valid lower bounds from ancestors to descendants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_0\supseteq A_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq A_k\) be a branch of search regions, and let each \(b_j\) satisfy \(b_j\le\inf_{x\in A_j}f(x)\). Since \(A_k\subseteq A_j\), every ancestral bound remains valid on the descendant: \[b_j\le\inf_{x\in A_k}f(x),\qquad 0\le j\le k.\] Hence the inherited bound \[b_k^{\mathrm{inh}}=\max_{0\le j\le k}b_j\] is a valid lower bound on \(A_k\). This inheritance requires only regional containment and validity, not inclusion-monotonicity of the bound-generation procedure.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq P\) be a child region. Suppose \(b_P\le\inf_{x\in P}f(x)\) is an inherited parent bound and \(\widetilde b_C\le\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\) is a newly recomputed valid child bound. Because \(C\subseteq P\), the inherited bound also satisfies \(b_P\le\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\). Therefore \[b_C=\max\{b_P,\widetilde b_C\}\] is valid for \(C\) and satisfies \(b_C\ge b_P\). knowledge_statements.title: Parent-to-Children Frontier Replacement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity of the aggregate bound after branching a frontier node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be an active frontier containing a parent \(P\), and replace \(P\) by children \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) that cover its feasible portion. Define \(F'=(F\setminus\{P\})\cup\{C_1,\ldots,C_m\}\). If every child satisfies \(L(C_i)\ge L(P)\), then \[\min_{R\in F'}L(R)\ge\min_{R\in F}L(R).\] Thus parent-to-children replacement cannot decrease the frontier lower bound. The coverage requirement preserves validity; child-bound dominance provides monotonicity. With incumbent accounting, the same conclusion holds after taking the minimum with the unchanged incumbent \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing a parent by covering children cannot lower the frontier aggregate when every child bound dominates the parent bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a nonempty feasible set, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) attain \(f^*=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\), and let \(U=f(\bar x)\) for some incumbent \(\bar x\in X\). A search region \(P\) may be removed when \(P\cap X=\varnothing\), or when it has a valid bound \(L(P)\le\inf_{x\in P\cap X}f(x)\) satisfying \(L(P)\ge U\). In the latter case, every feasible point in \(P\) has objective value at least \(U\). Let \(F\) be the finite remaining active frontier, suppose each \(R\in F\) has a valid bound \(L(R)\le\inf_{x\in R\cap X}f(x)\), and suppose the active and removed regions account for all of \(X\). If every removed region has one of the stated certificates, then \[L_{\mathrm{acct}}=\min\left(\{U\}\cup\{L(R):R\in F\}\right)\] satisfies \[L_{\mathrm{acct}}\le f^*\le U.\] If \(F=\varnothing\), then \(L_{\mathrm{acct}}=U=f^*\), certifying global optimality of the incumbent.

knowledge_statements.title: Ancestral Bound Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity correction for valid lower bounds along a branch-and-bound tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, let node \(v\) represent region \(R_v\), with \(R_v\subseteq R_{p(v)}\), and let \(\ell_v\le\inf_{x\in F\cap R_v}f(x)\) be its raw valid lower bound. Initialize \(L_r=\ell_r\) at the root. Process every nonroot node after its parent and set \[L_v=\max\{\ell_v,L_{p(v)}\}.\] Return \(L_v\) as the propagated bound. Because restriction cannot reduce the regional infimum, \(L_v\) remains valid and satisfies \(L_v\ge L_{p(v)}\). Thus each root-to-leaf sequence of propagated bounds is nondecreasing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace each raw node bound by its maximum with the propagated parent bound; validity is retained and ancestral monotonicity is enforced.
assumptions_latex: \(R_v\subseteq R_{p(v)}\) for every nonroot node \(v\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Running-maximum stabilization of successive valid bounds for a fixed or nested search region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a sequence of valid lower bounds \((\ell_k)_{k\ge0}\) for a common minimization target value \(m\), initialize \(L_0=\ell_0\) and update \[L_k=\max\{L_{k-1},\ell_k\}\quad(k\ge1).\] Equivalently, \(L_k=\max_{0\le j\le k}\ell_j\). Output \(L_k\) as the stabilized bound at iteration \(k\). If every \(\ell_k\le m\), then every \(L_k\le m\), while \(L_{k+1}\ge L_k\). For nested regions, the same update is valid when all retained earlier bounds apply to the current region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The running maximum of applicable valid lower bounds is itself valid and cannot decrease as computation proceeds.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell_k\le m\) for every \(k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Bound Recomputation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recomputation that accepts a node bound only after independently checkable validity certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization node with region \(R\), construct a relaxation whose feasible set \(Q(R)\) contains every representation of \(F\cap R\). Solve or bound the relaxation using certified arithmetic to obtain \(\widehat L\) together with a verifier-checkable certificate establishing \[\widehat L\le\inf_{y\in Q(R)}g(y).\] Verify both the containment claim and the bound certificate. If either verification fails, return no certified bound. Otherwise return \(L^{\mathrm{cert}}=\widehat L\), optionally stabilized as \(\max\{L^{\mathrm{cert}},L_{p}\}\) when the valid parent bound \(L_p\) applies. The accepted value is then a valid lower bound on \(F\cap R\).

Validity alone gives \(\widehat L_p\le \inf_{x\in F\cap R_p}f(x)\) and \(\widehat L_c\le \inf_{x\in F\cap R_c}f(x)\), but does not imply \(\widehat L_c\ge\widehat L_p\). knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Bound Reversal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rounding and solver error can reverse nearly equal parent and child computed bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let exact valid relaxation values satisfy \(L_c\ge L_p\), but let floating-point computations return \(\widehat L_p=L_p+e_p\) and \(\widehat L_c=L_c+e_c\). A reversal occurs precisely when \[e_p-e_c>L_c-L_p,\] because then \(\widehat L_c<\widehat L_p\). For example, \(L_p=1\), \(L_c=1+10^{-12}\), \(e_p=10^{-9}\), and \(e_c=-10^{-9}\) produce a reversal. knowledge_statements.title: Child-Region Coverage Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local feasible-coverage consequence of replacing a parent region by children, including empty and lower-dimensional children.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set, let \(R\) be a parent region, and let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) be children such that \(m\in\mathbb N\) and \(F\cap R=F\cap\bigcup_{j=1}^m C_j\). Let \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{new}}\) be the children retained as live and \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{new}}\) the children assigned valid removal certificates. knowledge_statements.title: Removed-Region Certificate Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage and nonloss invariant coupling every removed search region to a checkable safe-fathoming certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f\) over a feasible set \(F\). Let \(\mathcal L\) be the live regions, \(\mathcal D\) the removed regions, and \(\mathcal P\subseteq F\) a set of preserved feasible points. Define \(S=\mathcal P\cup\bigl(F\cap\bigcup_{R\in\mathcal L}R\bigr)\). A removed-region coverage certificate consists of \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{R\in\mathcal L\cup\mathcal D}R\) and, for every \(R\in\mathcal D\), a verifiable certificate that either \(F\cap R=\varnothing\) or \(\forall x\in F\cap R\;\exists y\in S\) such that \(f(y)\le f(x)\). Consequently, every feasible point is live or has a preserved feasible representative with no larger objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All feasible points are covered, and each removed region is certified either infeasible or dominated by feasible objective opportunities that remain preserved.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Objective Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Requirement that the incumbent bound use the original objective evaluated with certified numerical direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\in F\) be an incumbent for minimizing the original objective \(f\). Its stored bound \(U\) is valid when the evaluation procedure certifies \(U\ge f(\bar x)\). Exact evaluation permits \(U=f(\bar x)\); interval or directed-rounding evaluation may use the upper endpoint. A relaxation value, surrogate objective, or downward-rounded approximation cannot serve as \(U\) unless separately proved to dominate \(f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The incumbent bound must be an exact or upward-certified evaluation of the original objective, not an unvalidated surrogate or downward approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate-Feasibility Acceptance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions distinguishing heuristic tolerance feasibility from certified incumbent feasibility and rigorous upper-bound construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the exact feasible set, let \(F_\tau\supseteq F\) be a tolerance-enlarged set, and let \(\tilde x\in F_\tau\). Membership in \(F_\tau\) alone neither establishes \(\tilde x\in F\) nor makes \(f(\tilde x)\) a feasible-incumbent upper bound for minimizing over \(F\). The point \(\tilde x\) may be accepted as a certified incumbent only after validating \(\tilde x\in F\) and an upper enclosure \(U\ge f(\tilde x)\). Alternatively, if a repair produces \(\bar x\in F\) and \(U\ge f(\bar x)\), then \(\bar x\), rather than \(\tilde x\), supplies the incumbent. An independent rigorous upper bound may be used as a bound but does not by itself certify \(\tilde x\) as feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tolerance feasibility alone is heuristic. The candidate becomes a certified incumbent only after exact feasibility and objective validation; a repaired feasible point may instead become the incumbent, while an independent bound does not validate the original candidate.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Lower–Upper Bound Pairing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of a global objective bracket from live-region lower bounds and a validated incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=f(\bar x)\) for some \(\bar x\in F\). knowledge_statements.title: Absolute-Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive global optimality certificate for a feasible incumbent in a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\le f^*\le U\), where \(f^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\), and let \(U=f(\bar x)\) for a feasible incumbent \(\bar x\in F\). For a prescribed tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), if \(U-L\le\varepsilon\), then \(0\le f(\bar x)-f^*\le\varepsilon\). Thus the bound pair together with incumbent feasibility certifies that \(\bar x\) is an additive \(\varepsilon\)-global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the certified upper bound minus lower bound is at most epsilon, the feasible incumbent is globally optimal within additive epsilon.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f^\star\in\mathbb R\) be the global value of a minimization problem, and let \(L,U\in\mathbb R\) satisfy \(L\le f^\star\le U\). Define \(s=\max\{1,|U|,|L|\}\) and \(\rho=(U-L)/s\). The data \((L,U)\) form an \(\varepsilon\)-relative-gap certificate when \(\rho\le\varepsilon\). Validity of the bounds then yields \(0\le U-f^\star\le U-L\le\varepsilon s\). Thus the certified incumbent value is globally accurate under the stated symmetric scaling convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid global bounds certify relative accuracy when their difference is at most the tolerance times the chosen symmetric objective scale.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^{\star}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\) and \(\mathcal C_k^{\star}=\{C\in\mathcal C_k:C\cap X^{\star}\ne\varnothing\}\). The algorithm has finite identification when there exists \(K<\infty\) such that, for every \(k\ge K\), the solution-bearing family is unchanged: \(\mathcal C_k^{\star}=\mathcal C_K^{\star}\). Every region outside this family is then permanently discarded, while the retained family continues to cover \(X^{\star}\). This notion concerns finite identification of optimal regions, not necessarily finite production of an exact optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite identification occurs when, after some iteration, the algorithm permanently rejects all nonoptimal candidate regions and its collection of regions containing global minimizers no longer changes.

children.title: Refinement Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity attributable to the depth, frequency, or granularity of regional refinement.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) has finite diameter \(D\).
A refinement rule replaces any selected region of diameter \(d\) by at most \(b\ge2\) children of diameter at most \(\rho d\), where \(0<\rho<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case geometric refinement count under uniform contraction and bounded branching.

source_refs.locator: 1.5 Complexity Analysis p. 19

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After depth \(k\), every descendant region has diameter at most \(D\rho^k\). Hence diameter at most \(\varepsilon\in(0,D)\) is guaranteed by depth \(k_{\varepsilon}=\left\lceil\log(D/\varepsilon)/\log(1/\rho)\right\rceil\). If no region is pruned, a full refinement tree contains at most \(b^{k_{\varepsilon}}\) regions at that depth and at most \((b^{k_{\varepsilon}+1}-1)/(b-1)\) regions through that depth. These are worst-case region counts, excluding the cost of evaluating bounds within a region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform contraction reaches diameter epsilon after logarithmically many refinement levels, but bounded branching can make the total number of generated regions exponential in that depth.
knowledge_statements.title: Refinement Complexity

children.title: Covering Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity attributable to maintaining a sufficient regional cover for certification.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a compact metric space.
An evaluation at \(x_i\) validates the method only on the closed ball \(\overline B(x_i,r)\) of fixed radius \(r>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m\ge N(X,r)\), and \(m=N(X,r)\) is achievable by a minimum covering

notation.meaning: minimum number of radius-r balls covering X

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluation lower bound when each sample certifies only one fixed-radius metric neighborhood.

source_refs.locator: 3.1.1 Covering with Balls and Optimization p. 94
2. Covering Methods p. 25

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(N(X,r)=\min\{m:X\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^{m}\overline B(x_i,r),\ x_i\in X\}\). Any deterministic procedure whose \(i\)-th evaluation certifies validity only on \(\overline B(x_i,r)\) requires at least \(N(X,r)\) evaluations to certify all of \(X\). Conversely, evaluating at the centers of a minimum radius-\(r\) cover gives global coverage using exactly \(N(X,r)\) evaluations, provided the stated local certificate is valid at every selected center.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When one evaluation certifies only a radius-r neighborhood, globally certifying the search space requires at least its radius-r covering number, and a minimum cover attains that count.

knowledge_statements.title: Refinement–Covering Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison between geometric refinement depth and an upper bound on the size of a complete metric cover at the attained scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\varepsilon\le\min\{D,r_0\}\), uniform contraction reaches diameter at most \(\varepsilon\) by depth \(k_{\varepsilon}=\left\lceil\log(D/\varepsilon)/\log(1/\rho)\right\rceil=O(\!\left(\log(1/\varepsilon)\right)\). The covering-number assumption guarantees a radius-\(\varepsilon\) cover containing at most \(C\varepsilon^{-q}\) balls. At the depth scale \(\varepsilon_k=D\rho^k\), this upper bound becomes \(N(X,\varepsilon_k)\le CD^{-q}\rho^{-qk}\). Thus logarithmic refinement depth is compatible with an exponentially larger upper bound in depth for the size of a complete cover; these bounds alone do not establish the number of regions actually generated or a matching lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform contraction reaches accuracy epsilon in logarithmically many levels, while the assumed covering estimate guarantees a complete cover of at most polynomial size in inverse epsilon, equivalently an exponential upper bound in refinement depth. This comparison does not determine actual algorithmic work or provide a matching lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is compact and \(N(X,r)\le Cr^{-q}\) for constants \(C>0\), \(q\ge0\), and every \(0<r\le r_0\).
An initial region has diameter at most \(D>0\), and each refinement step reduces descendant diameter by a factor of at most \(\rho\in(0,1)\).

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is compact and has packing numbers \(M(X,2r)\).
Each oracle query can certify validity only within distance \(r\) of its query point.

notation.meaning: maximum cardinality of a set with pairwise distances greater than 2r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp loss of deterministic full-space coverage below the metric covering number.

source_refs.locator: 3.1.1 Covering with Balls and Optimization p. 94

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For query points \(x_1,\ldots,x_T\in X\), deterministic coverage fails whenever \(T<N(X,r)\), because then \(X\nsubseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^{T}\overline B(x_i,r)\). Consequently some point remains uncertified. Moreover \(M(X,2r)\le N(X,r)\): any radius-\(r\) ball contains at most one member of a set whose pairwise distances exceed \(2r\). Hence such a packing supplies an explicit lower bound on the number of local certificates required for complete coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Below the radius-r covering number, some search-space point necessarily remains uncertified; a separated packing provides a concrete lower bound on this coverage threshold.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Evaluation Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive accounting for formulation, relaxation solution, and numerical validation across evaluated node bounds in a fixed computational model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a machine or arithmetic-operation model. For evaluated node \(i\), let \(T_{\mathrm{form},i}\), \(T_{\mathrm{solve},i}\), and \(T_{\mathrm{validate},i}\) be the costs of the three sequential phases comprising its certified bound evaluation, and define \(T_{\mathrm{node},i}=T_{\mathrm{form},i}+T_{\mathrm{solve},i}+T_{\mathrm{validate},i}\). For \(N\ge1\) evaluated nodes, the total bound-evaluation cost satisfies \(T_{\mathrm{bound}}=\sum_{i=1}^{N}T_{\mathrm{node},i}\le N\max_{1\le i\le N}T_{\mathrm{node},i}\). This accounting excludes branching, node selection, and incumbent evaluation unless their costs are explicitly included in one of the three phases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a fixed computational model, each certified node-bound cost is the sum of formulation, solution, and validation costs. Across N evaluated nodes, total bound work is at most N times the largest evaluated-node cost; unrelated branch-and-bound operations are excluded unless explicitly included.
assumptions_latex: A fixed computational model is used, and \(N\ge1\) node relaxations are evaluated.
For each evaluated node \(i\), formulation, solution to the requested accuracy, and validation are sequential phases whose costs account for the entire certified bound evaluation.

total certified bound-evaluation cost over all evaluated nodes

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Verification Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-complexity criterion for checking a supplied finite relaxation-validity certificate in a fixed certificate language.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix finite encodings, a certificate language, and an exact deterministic verifier that is sound for the claimed bound or relaxation-validity relation. If an instance has encoding length \(s\) and a supplied certificate has encoding length \(m\), let \(T_{\mathrm{verify}}(s,m)\) be the verifier's worst-case number of bit operations over well-formed pairs of those lengths. Verification is polynomial-time when constants \(C>0\) and \(c\ge0\) exist such that \(T_{\mathrm{verify}}(s,m)\le C(s+m+1)^c\) for all well-formed pairs. This bound concerns checking a supplied certificate and does not bound certificate construction or guarantee that every valid instance has a certificate of polynomial length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed certificate language and sound exact verifier, verification complexity is the worst-case bit-operation count for checking a supplied instance-certificate pair. Verification is polynomial when this count is bounded by a constant times a fixed power of the combined encoding length; this says nothing about finding certificates or their possible lengths.
assumptions_latex: A finite instance encoding, finite certificate language, and exact deterministic verifier are fixed.
The verifier is sound for the claimed bound or relaxation-validity relation, and \(s,m\in\mathbb N\) are the instance and certificate encoding lengths.

notation.meaning: worst-case verifier bit complexity for well-formed pairs of lengths s and m
